intro: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Google added Gemini 4 Neon, and Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq in the same week. The Lean and Mathlib communities certified a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, while critical flaws in NGINX, OpenSSL and Rails kept security teams busy.

top.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol
top.body: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol for fast everyday tasks. Astra costs $8 input and $40 output per million tokens, 20% below its predecessor; Sol costs $2 input and $10 output.

top.title: Anthropic prices IPO and starts trading on Nasdaq
top.body: Anthropic published a post about the pricing of its initial public offering. Reuters covered the Nasdaq debut.

top.title: Lean and Mathlib communities certify a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
top.body: The Lean and Mathlib communities published a joint statement on 2026-11-21. The statement certifies a Lean library (about 17 million lines) released by Levent Alpöge on 2026-11-20.

top.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon: 1M context, $3/$15 per 1M tokens
top.body: Google released Gemini 4 Neon on 2026-11-18. It has a 1M-token context window.

top.title: Two critical NGINX HTTP/2 flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution
top.body: Wiz reports CVE-2026-123633 (HTTP/2 use-after-free) and CVE-2026-123007 (HTTP/2 send_window integer underflow), both CVSS 4.0 score 9.2. Both need HTTP/2 enabled.

top.title: OpenSSL fixes critical buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock (CVE-2026-121481)
top.body: OpenSSL published a fix for a buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock(). The CVE is CVE-2026-121481 and the CVSS score is 9.8.

top.title: Vera Rubin NVL72 sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1 in its debut
top.body: NVIDIA posted the top result on every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and was the only platform to submit them all. Vera Rubin NVL72 gave up to 2x the performance per GPU of GB300 NVL72.

top.title: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max in managed preview
top.body: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max as a managed preview on November 16. Access is through the Token Plan API for coding agents, QwenWork, Qoder, the Qwen App and QwenStudio.

top.title: Claude solves two open black-hole physics problems
top.body: Anthropic's Science team reports that Claude Fable 5.2 completed a 2003 Hawking-Page calculation in N=4 super Yang-Mills theory. It also found the exact optimal ceiling of the modular bootstrap for 3D gravity (about c/9.1266) and verified it formally in Lean.

top.title: Optimizely snippets served malware on Zoom, GitLab and 176 other sites
top.body: On 16 November an attacker wrote malicious code into the Project JavaScript field of Optimizely Web projects. Report URI found infected snippets for 178 organisations, including Zoom, BBC, Salesforce, GitLab and HSBC.

chips.title: NVIDIA unveils Rubin HPC GPU with 50,000+ CUDA cores
chips.body: At SC26 NVIDIA announced Rubin HPC, which puts more than 50,000 CUDA cores on one GPU, a record by NVIDIA's count.

chips.title: OpenAI models find up to 14% PPA gains in AMD GPU IP
chips.body: OpenAI says its models rewrote circuit code for AMD's flagship GPU IP and found up to 14% power, performance and area gains over heavily optimized baselines in under five months.

chips.title: Frostbite: Architect Labs reports an AI-designed CPU with new ISA
chips.body: Architect Labs says its AI systems designed and verified Frostbite, a CPU with a new instruction set based on interaction nets.

skill_of_week.name: rust-anything
skill_of_week.what: rust-anything helps a coding agent rewrite an app in Rust and proves that the rewrite behaves like the original. It records the original app's outputs, errors and side effects on generated edge cases, generates a Rust crate with a wrapper that keeps the original API, and replays every recorded case against the Rust code. Nothing ships until all cases match. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java and Kotlin, with whole-app record and replay for PHP and C#.
skill_of_week.verdict: Worth a try for hot paths
skill_of_week.note: It gained about 4,600 stars this week, and version 2.0 ported Prettier to Rust with Claude Code. It is MIT licensed and has test fixtures, but it is a one-person project. It catches only the behavior that the recording covers, and per-call overhead can make small Rust functions slower than a JIT, so target hot loops. The record and replay commands run your code many times: use a copy of the project, a test database and no production credentials. Agent token cost grows with the number of units you port.
